## Purpose

Worker profiles turns 1 named worker profile into the exact CLI, flags, environment, config files and sandbox of each agent launch, so that every agent runs on the operator's subscription logins and never with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (C2). It serves ideas and task-execution, which ask it for a launch environment before every launch. It keeps the adapters of every agent CLI correct by docs sync and conformance tests, and marks a profile unhealthy when its adapter fails. It does not start processes (fleet-runtime) and does not choose which task runs (task-execution).

## Strategic classification

| Domain | Business model | Evolution |
|---|---|---|
| supporting | compliance-enforcer | custom |

_Strategize rationale_: supporting - G4 needs a fallback persona for every worker persona and G1 needs a liveness feed from each CLI; today's alternative is the teammates roster and agent CLIs run by hand; rule 3 (diff 5); cplx 4 from mapping 1 profile to the flags, environment and files of each CLI and from conformance tests. Medium investment because it owns the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY scrub (C2) and the CLIs change every week (C10). — _future_: Supporting, kept as 1 adapter per CLI behind 1 profile shape. If the agent CLIs converge on 1 headless protocol, adapters move to transaction-script glue.

## Domain roles

**enforcer** — Every launch of every context passes through its launch-environment query, which applies the environment scrub and the login rules (decompose N2, connect N3). It ensures that other contexts carry out the operator's credential rule: an enforcer. It owns 1 aggregate, the worker profile, with few commands.

## Ubiquitous language

| Term | Meaning in this context | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| **Worker Profile** | The teammate file of 1 persona: agent CLI, model, effort, skills, MCP servers, sandbox, writable paths, network, liveness, retry and fallback. Profile is its short name. | — |
| **Adapter** | The code for 1 agent CLI that turns a worker profile into the exact flags, environment and files of a launch, and reads its quota and context. | — |
| **Persona** | A named worker profile that a plan task names. Every worker persona names a fallback persona on another provider when the roster has one. | — |
| **Conformance** | The test that launches 1 adapter and reads back its effective settings (sandbox, context limit, hooks, scrubbed environment). A pass makes the profile healthy. | — |
| **Profile** | A named worker profile: the CLI, model, effort, sandbox and permission rules that 1 attempt runs with | — |
| **Healthy** | A profile whose adapter passed its last conformance test. Dispatch does not choose an unhealthy profile | — |
| **Launch environment** | The exact CLI, flags, scrubbed environment, config home files and sandbox profile that worker-profiles resolves for 1 process launch. Coined in connect (assumption A6) | — |

## Business decisions

1. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is removed from the environment of every launch: attempt, sub-orchestrator pane, detached child, updater and probe. The roster rejects a teammate file that sets it (05 E-10, 06 S1, understand N16, decompose N2).
2. agy children lose GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY and GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL, and the roster rejects them (06 S3). Secrets reach agents only through env vars that the profile names, never through task files (SR-2).
3. A profile must declare CLI, model, skills, MCP servers, sandbox, writable paths, context budget, timeouts and restart policy, and every worker persona must name a fallback persona; the roster refuses an incomplete profile (FR-6).
4. A sandboxed persona does not start on a host that cannot sandbox it (06 S9). Each worker writes only to its task directory, its worktree and the paths its profile names (SR-1).
5. When an adapter conformance test fails, its profile is marked unhealthy, and dispatch does not choose an unhealthy profile until a conformance test passes. A waiting_approval stall also marks the profile unhealthy.
6. The private CODEX_HOME links every entry of the real codex home except rules/, the Prime agent dir links auth.json, and every codex launch gets --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust (06 S4, S5, S6). Trust writes stay narrow (06 S10).
7. A new agent CLI release is used only after the update cooldown of more than 1 week; a CLI with unreadable release dates is held back. Pane auto-update stays off for claude and codex (06 S7, S8, C10).
8. Each agent runs with a context limit of 256k tokens, set through the CLI's own setting where one exists; else the wrapper ends the attempt with a handoff at 256k (FR-9). The OpenCode, pi and Prime adapters carry over (06 S15).

## Assumptions

- [discover A3] Daemon supervision (stale heartbeat, restart, self-update) and adapter conformance are cross-cutting. They sit at the end of the executing phase (sequence 540 to 580, before Task Done) because they act on running attempts. Decision D2 records the alternatives. (confidence medium)
- [decompose A4] Worker profiles and adapters are their own context because of their rate of change and their credential rules, although the storm holds only 2 of their events (discover H14). Open decision D3. (confidence medium)
- [strategize A6] Worker profiles is supporting with medium investment because it owns the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY scrub (C2, an absolute operator rule). Its complexity is the rate of change of the agent CLIs, not domain rules. (confidence high)
- [connect A1] All 6 contexts run in the 1 fleetd process, so every context-to-context message is in-process. Only the command channel, the file protocol, the herdr adapter, the platform layer, git and GitHub cross a process boundary (design: Architecture and roles). (confidence high)
- [organise A4] The data store is 1 SQLite ledger (~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3, WAL) plus the workspace files, both owned by the 1 deployable. Inside the ledger each context owns its tables: ideas owns ideas, requirements, questions; task-execution owns tasks, task_deps, task_covers, attempts, leases; worktree-custody owns worktrees; integration owns features, branches, gate_runs, trial_merges; fleet-runtime owns events and ingested; worker-profiles owns no table (its profiles are teammate files). Source: design Ledger schema with the aggregates of discover and decompose. (confidence medium)
- [organise A6] herdr, the agent CLIs, git, GitHub and the OS service managers are external systems behind adapters in fleet-runtime and the other owning contexts. None is a deployable of this design (strategize N1; design: Architecture and roles). (confidence high)
- [organise A8] Each context owns its workspace folders inside the 1 deployable: ideas owns the idea folders (ai_docs/plans/<run>/, design /fleet/ideas/), task-execution owns the task and attempt folders under the state root, worker-profiles owns the teammate profile files (understand N17; design: Workspace layout and file protocol). (confidence medium)
- [define A12] 'conformist' guessed for external system clock (core contexts protect their model; others conform) - confirm
- [define A17] Business model compliance-enforcer.

## Verification metrics

- Business (C2): count of child processes, panes, probes or updaters started with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in their environment. Target 0.
- Business (G1): count of attempts dispatched on an unhealthy profile. Target 0.
- Structural: count of process launches that do not take their environment from launch-environment (connect N3). Target 0.

## Open questions

- [discover Q4] Where on the timeline does daemon supervision and adapter conformance belong: in executing, in its own phase, or off the idea timeline (D2)?
- [decompose Q2] Docs sync and adapter conformance are stormed as 2 events only (discover H14). Which context turns a drift into a task, and how does a profile become healthy again?
- [connect Q1] Which context owns the fleet-run wrapper: task-execution, worker-profiles or fleet-runtime (decision D2)?
- [discover H14 near adapter-conformance-failed - missing] Docs sync and adapter conformance are collapsed to 2 events here. The flow that turns a drift into a task (who owns it, how a profile becomes healthy again) is not stormed.
